title: Denaturing SUMO Immunoprecipitation From Mitotic Cells
author: Alexandra K. Walker

steps.title: Plate U2OS cells
steps.instruction: Plate 2 × 10⁶ U‑2 OS cells per 150 mm² dish (4 dishes) in complete growth medium and incubate 37 °C, 5 % CO₂, humidified for 3 days until 70‑80 % confluence.

steps.title: Add nocodazole and incubate
steps.instruction: Replace medium with 25 mL pre‑warmed complete medium containing 100 ng/mL nocodazole per dish and incubate 16 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Check mitotic enrichment
steps.instruction: Examine dishes under a light microscope; rounded cells indicate mitosis. Handle dishes gently to avoid detaching mitotic cells.

steps.title: Harvest mitotic cells by shake‑off
steps.instruction: Collect mitotic cells from each dish using repeated washes:

substeps.instruction: Aspirate media into a 25 mL pipette, tap dish bottom three times, return half the media to the dish and place the other half in a 50 mL centrifuge tube.
Using a 10 mL pipette, draw up the remaining media and gently wash the dish surface repeatedly (4–6 washes) to detach all rounded cells into suspension.
Check under the microscope that no asynchronous cells have detached; if rounded cells remain, repeat washes.
Pool the media containing mitotic cells from each dish into the same 50 mL tube (total from 2 × 150 mm² dishes per tube, continue for all dishes).

steps.title: Count cells and normalize
steps.instruction: Mix pooled suspension, take 10 µL into a counting chamber, determine cell number for each sample and adjust the volume of each suspension so that all samples contain an equal number of cells.

steps.title: Pellet cells and wash
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 300 × g for 5 min (room temperature), discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 1 mL PBS, transfer to labeled 1.5 mL microtubes, centrifuge 300 × g for 5 min at 4 °C, discard PBS. (Pause point: pellets can be snap‑frozen at –80 °C for ≤2 weeks; thaw on ice before proceeding.)

steps.title: Lyse cells in 1 % SDS buffer
steps.instruction: Flick tubes to disrupt pellets, add 200 µL 1 % SDS lysis buffer, incubate on ice 10 min (viscous lysate).

steps.title: Sonicate lysate
steps.instruction: Sonicate 5 s on, 10 s on ice; repeat for a total of 4 × 5 s cycles using a Microson XL 2000 (22.5 kHz, probe intensity 10).

steps.title: Add DTT and reduce
steps.instruction: Add 10 µL of 1 M DTT (final 50 mM) to each sample and incubate on ice 30 min.

steps.title: Clarify lysate by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 14,000 × g for 15 min in a refrigerated centrifuge set to 4 °C; collect the supernatant.

steps.title: Prepare input for western
steps.instruction: Remove 30 µL supernatant, add to 60 µL loading buffer, mix, boil 5 min at 95 °C, store at –20 °C (input for later immunoblot).

steps.title: Equalize lysate volumes
steps.instruction: Measure remaining supernatant volume; adjust so each sample contains the same volume (target 150 µL).

steps.title: Dilute lysate 1:10
steps.instruction: Add ice‑cold 0 % SDS lysis buffer to bring each sample to 1.5 mL total (final SDS 0.1 %).

steps.title: Clarify diluted lysate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 14,000 × g for 15 min, 4 °C; keep the clarified supernatant.

steps.title: Pool lysates
steps.instruction: Combine all clarified supernatants into a single 15 mL centrifuge tube and keep on ice until bead preparation.

steps.title: Wash protein A/G beads
steps.instruction: Prepare beads for antibody coupling:

substeps.instruction: Vortex Pierce protein A/G agarose beads 2–3 s to suspend.
Cut the tip of a 200 µL pipette tip, aliquot 30 µL beads into each of three 1.5 mL tubes.
Add 300 µL 0.1 % SDS buffer, vortex, centrifuge 500 × g 1 min, discard supernatant leaving ~10–20 µL; repeat wash two more times.
Add 1 mL 0.1 % SDS buffer to each tube, vortex to resuspend.

steps.title: Couple SUMO antibodies to beads
steps.instruction: Add antibodies to beads:

substeps.instruction: Add 3 µg SUMO1 antibody to tube 1.
Add 3 µg SUMO2/3 antibody to tube 2.
Place the three tubes into a 50 mL centrifuge tube and roll at 15–25 rpm, room temperature, 1 h.

steps.title: Collect antibody‑bound beads
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the bead tubes 500 × g for 1 min, discard supernatant.

steps.title: Incubate lysate with antibody beads
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL diluted lysate to each bead tube, place tubes in a 50 mL tube, roll at 15–25 rpm, 4 °C, overnight.

steps.title: Pellet beads after IP
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 500 × g for 1 min, 4 °C; discard supernatant carefully.

steps.title: Wash beads three times
steps.instruction: Perform three washes:

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL ice‑cold 0.1 % SDS buffer, invert 2–3×, roll 15–25 rpm, room temperature, 3 min.
Repeat the above wash two more times.

steps.title: Add loading buffer to beads
steps.instruction: Remove residual buffer, add 30 µL loading buffer directly to bead pellet, vortex or flick to mix.

steps.title: Boil samples
steps.instruction: Heat samples at 95 °C for 10 min; optionally place a weighted heat‑resistant object on tubes to prevent lid opening.

steps.title: Thaw input sample
steps.instruction: Retrieve frozen input (step 12) from –20 °C, thaw on ice.

steps.title: Centrifuge boiled samples
steps.instruction: Spin at 14,000 × g for 5 min at room temperature; collect supernatant for SDS‑PAGE.

steps.title: Assemble gradient gels
steps.instruction: Set up two 4‑20 % Tris‑Glycine mini gels in a mini‑gel tank and fill with 1× running buffer.

steps.title: Load ladder, input, IP samples
steps.instruction: Load 5 µL protein ladder and 15 µL input into the first lane of each gel; load ½ of the supernatant from each bead condition (negative, SUMO1, SUMO2/3) into subsequent lanes, avoiding bead pellets.

steps.title: Run gels
steps.instruction: Run at constant 220 V for 45 min.

steps.title: Transfer proteins to PVDF
steps.instruction: Activate a 7 × 9 cm PVDF membrane with methanol, assemble transfer cassette, and transfer in a cold room or ice bucket at 100 V for 3 h using pre‑chilled 1× transfer buffer.

steps.title: Block membranes with milk
steps.instruction: Incubate each membrane in 5 mL 5 % milk in PBST for 30 min at room temperature, rolling 15–25 rpm.

steps.title: Incubate with primary antibodies
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL SUMO1 antibody to the SUMO1 membrane tube and 5 µL SUMO2/3 antibody to the SUMO2/3 membrane tube; incubate overnight at 4 °C, rolling 15–25 rpm.

steps.title: Wash membranes after primary
steps.instruction: Wash membranes 5 min in 5 mL PBST, rolling 15–25 rpm; repeat three times.

steps.title: Incubate with HRP secondary
steps.instruction: Dilute appropriate HRP‑conjugated secondary antibody 1:5,000 in 5 % milk, add to membranes, and incubate 1 h at room temperature, rolling 15–25 rpm.

steps.title: Wash membranes after secondary
steps.instruction: Wash membranes 5 min in 5 mL PBST, rolling 15–25 rpm; repeat three times.

steps.title: Apply ECL and expose
steps.instruction: Mix ECL reagents per manufacturer, cover each 7 × 9 cm membrane with 1 mL ECL, dab excess, place membrane face‑down on cling film, seal, insert into developing cassette, expose X‑ray film in a dark room (vary exposure times 0–30 min as needed), develop film, label and scan as TIFF.

description: Validation of protocol This protocol is an optimized version of the one used and validated, with the adaptations listed below, in the following research article: • Lanz et al. [7]. HDAC6-dependent deacetylation of SAE2 enhances SUMO1 conjugation for mitotic integrity. EMBO J . (Figure 3A and EV4F). The adaptations used for this research article were applied to address the specific research question under investigation (not fundamental to the assay’s performance). These adaptations were the use of doxycycline-inducible cell lines that expressed SAE1:SAE2 constructs resistant to the SUMO E1 inhibitor ML792, the concurrent addition of doxycycline and ML792 with nocodazole treatment, and the release of nocodazole into fresh media containing doxycycline and ML792 for 10 min before harvesting. In Figure 3A from [7], the immunoprecipitation for SUMO1 was performed using the antibody described here, but the western blot was probed using ab133352. Free SUMO1 in Figure EV4F from [7] was detected by using ab320580, as it can detect both free and conjugated forms of SUMO1. Validation of mitotic cell enrichment, following mitotic shake-off (described in section A), was performed via western blotting ( Figure 2 ). Figure 2. Validation of mitotic enrichment following nocodazole treatment and shake-off. The blot displays Cyclin B1 levels in lysates made from either an asynchronous cell population (Async) or cells treated with 100 ng/mL nocodazole for 16 h and harvested via mitotic shake-off (Mitotic). α Tubulin and Histone H3 are included as loading controls. This representative image was obtained from one biological repeat.
